title: 4.10.7 Select multiple
body:
If the multiple attribute is present, options not disabled shall indicate select-ability using checkboxes placed in the same location as the user agent's behavior for it's menu item checkmarks.

The user agent may replace the select with a shadow document of label wrapped checkboxes as long as the default platform select behavior remains:

Drag selection, keyboard click selection, and keyboard navigation remain the same with the exception that a single item selection does not reset the selected set of options to that single item but adds or subtracts the item from the selectedOptions. Platform shortcuts for select all and select none shall also be supported. When an option is in focus an activate action (such as spacebar or enter) checks or unchecks the checkbox while adding or removing the item from the selectedOptions.

Why? Because Mozilla refused until HTML5 said something. Editors back a decade ago said they'd wait for browsers.

Accessibility has been difficult:
1. Disabled people have difficulty with key+click operations.
2. Users are not even informed multiple selection is possible unless the label does so.
3. Users do not know control click selection (Apple users use command click; phones?) 
4. Shift click does a range selection, if they users even know about it.

Checkbox sets are CLEAR indicators and are familiar and a scroll box of checkboxes is not uncommon in Apps. All specifics of CSS etc can be lifted from input checkboxes as well as initial implementations using a shadow document to implement the change. Background compatibility is moot, this is merely a UI bug fix.
